reason: Both sell subscription cloud software with AI lead scoring and prioritization that helps businesses win customers. Thryv sells an SMB CRM and done-for-you marketing platform to local service businesses. ZoomInfo sells a B2B contact database and sales intelligence to sales and marketing teams at companies of all sizes. The product overlap is only in lead generation and CRM-style workflows. The customers are mostly different: local SMBs versus B2B revenue teams. Thryv also has marketing services and legacy print directories, which ZoomInfo lacks. That is partial overlap, not a direct match.
